title: The completion of a flat local p-adic algebra with maximal ideal (p) is a DVR
statement: Let $p$ be prime, and let $S$ be a commutative local ring with a flat ring map $\varphi:\mathbf Z_p\to S$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and maximal ideal $pS$. Its fixed completion $A=\varprojlim_n S/(p^nS)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is an integral domain and a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. No assertion about an arbitrarily prescribed field or existence of a new underlying ring is made.

source.place: Tag 0328, proof after choosing the flat local extension; Tag 00PD, unit-times-uniformizer-power argument. Direct cancellation in completion components replaces the source's complete-flatness and dimension arguments.

proof.text: Flatness over the domain `ℤ_[p]` makes multiplication by `p` injective on `S`: tensor the injective multiplication map on `ℤ_[p]` with `S`. Write `A` for the explicit completion `AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal S) S`.

The maximal ideal of `S` is the principal ideal `(p)`, hence finitely generated. The completion results of Tag 05GG make `A` complete and local, with maximal ideal `(p)` and nonzero field quotient `S/(p)`.

Multiplication by `p` is injective on `A` directly. If `p*x = 0`, choose a lift `y` of the component of `x` in `S/(p^(n+1))`. Then `p*y = p^(n+1)*z` for some `z` in `S`. Cancel `p` using step 1 to get `y = p^n*z`. Thus the component of `x` in `S/(p^n)` is zero for every `n`; componentwise equality gives `x = 0`.

Separatedness says that an element in every `(p)^n` is zero. For nonzero `x`, the set of `n` for which `x` belongs to `(p)^n` is a nonempty bounded initial segment of the natural numbers: choose a power not containing `x`, and use the decreasing filtration. Take its largest member `n` and write `x = p^n*u`. If `u` were a nonunit, locality would put it in `(p)`, contradicting maximality.

Products of two nonzero elements are `p^(n+m)` times a unit. They are nonzero by step 3 and nontriviality of `A`; hence `A` is a domain. The element `p` is nonzero by step 3 and is a nonunit since it is in the maximal ideal. Its principal ideal is maximal, so `p` is prime, hence irreducible in the domain.

Every nonzero ideal contains an element of least exponent in step 4. This element generates the ideal because all other elements are divisible by its power of `p`, and its unit factor is invertible. Thus every ideal is principal. The nonzero nonunit `p` shows that `A` is not a field. Together with locality and the domain property this is precisely a discrete valuation ring.

proof_origin.place: Adaptation of the completion construction in Tag 0328 and valuation factorization in Tag 00PD; injectivity on the completion proved directly by cancellation of p on successive quotient components.

theorem adicCompletion_dvr_of_flat_padicInt (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing S] (φ : ℤ_[p] →+* S)
    (hFlat : φ.Flat) (hMax : IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S = Ideal.span {(p : S)}) :
    ∃ (_ : IsDomain (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S) S)),
      IsDiscreteValuationRing (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S) S)
